\(A\,B^{T}=|A|I\).

Taking determinants,

\(\det(B)=\det(B^{T})=|A|^2\).

Hence

\(\det(AB)=\det(A)\det(B)=|A|^3\).

So it is enough to find \(|A|\).

Using the cofactor \(C_{12}=-9\),

\(C_{12}
=-\begin{vmatrix}
\alpha & \beta\\
-\beta & 2\alpha

\end{vmatrix}\)

Using the cofactor \(C_{11}=3\alpha\),

\(C_{11}
=\begin{vmatrix}
\alpha & \beta\\
\alpha & 2\alpha
\end{vmatrix}\)

\(=\alpha(2\alpha-\beta)\)

\(=3\alpha\).

\(\beta=2\alpha-3\).

Substituting in

\(2\alpha^2+\beta^2=9\),

\(2\alpha^2+(2\alpha-3)^2=9\),

\(6\alpha^2-12\alpha=0\),

\(|A|

1&2&3\\
2&2&1\\
-1&2&4
\end{vmatrix}\)

\(=1(8-2)-2(8+1)+3(4+2)\)

\(=6-18+18\)

\(=6\).

Let \(S_1=\{z \in C:|z| \leq 5\}, S_2=\left\{z \in C: \operatorname{Im}\left(\frac{z+1-\sqrt{3} i}{1-\sqrt{3} i}\right) \geq 0\right\}\) and \(S_3=\{z \in C: \operatorname{Re}(z) \geq 0\}\). Then the area of the region \(S_1 \cap S_2 \cap S_3\) is: 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\), where \(x,y\in\mathbb R\).

The set \(S_1\) is given by \(|z|\leq5\).

Therefore, \(S_1\) is the closed disc \(x^2+y^2\leq25\).

For \(S_2\), consider \(\dfrac{z+1-\sqrt3i}{1-\sqrt3i}\).

Multiply its numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(1+\sqrt3i\).

We get \(\dfrac{(x+1+i(y-\sqrt3))(1+\sqrt3i)}{(1-\sqrt3i)(1+\sqrt3i)}\).

The denominator is \(1+3=4\), which is positive.

Expanding the numerator, its imaginary part is \(\sqrt3(x+1)+(y-\sqrt3)=\sqrt3x+y\).

Therefore, \(\operatorname{Im}\left(\dfrac{z+1-\sqrt3i}{1-\sqrt3i}\right)\geq0\) is equivalent to \(\sqrt3x+y\geq0\).

Hence \(S_2\) is the half-plane \(y\geq-\sqrt3x\).

The set \(S_3\) is given by \(\operatorname{Re}(z)\geq0\), so \(x\geq0\).

Use polar coordinates \(x=r\cos\theta\) and \(y=r\sin\theta\).

The condition \(x\geq0\) gives \(-\dfrac\pi2\leq\theta\leq\dfrac\pi2\).

The condition \(y\geq-\sqrt3x\) gives \(\sin\theta+\sqrt3\cos\theta\geq0\).

Since \(\sin\theta+\sqrt3\cos\theta=2\sin\left(\theta+\dfrac\pi3\right)\), this gives \(-\dfrac\pi3\leq\theta\leq\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\).

The common angular interval is \(-\dfrac\pi3\leq\theta\leq\dfrac\pi2\).

Its angle is \(\dfrac\pi2+\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\).

Therefore, the required region is a sector of radius \(5\) and angle \(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\).

Its area is \(\dfrac12r^2\theta=\dfrac12(5)^2\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{125\pi}{12}\).

Hence the correct option is \(\mathrm{A}\).

\(x^2+y^2-2a(x+y)=0\).

Let \(\frac{dy}{dx}=y'\).

Hence, \(a=\frac{x+yy'}{1+y'}\).

From the circle equation,

So, \((x^2-2xy-y^2)y'+y^2-x^2-2xy=0\).

Therefore, \((x^2-2xy-y^2)\frac{dy}{dx}=x^2+2xy-y^2\).

Let \(g(x)=2+x-2x^2\).

Now, \(g'(x)=1-4x\).

Let \(b=\dfrac1a\).

\(2+b-2b^2=0\).

Hence, \(2b^2-b-2=0\).

questions.question:
Let the maximum and minimum values of \(\left(\sqrt{8 x-x^2-12}-4\right)^2+(x-7)^2, x \in R\) be \(M\) and \(m\), respectively. Then M2-m2 is equal to  _______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The square root is real only when \(8x-x^2-12\geq0\).

We have \(8x-x^2-12=4-(x-4)^2\).

Therefore, \(4-(x-4)^2\geq0\), which gives \((x-4)^2\leq4\).

Hence \(2\leq x\leq6\).

Put \(y=\sqrt{8x-x^2-12}\).

Then \(y\geq0\) and \(y^2=4-(x-4)^2\).

Therefore, \((x-4)^2+y^2=4\).

Thus \((x,y)\) lies on the upper semicircle with centre \((4,0)\) and radius \(2\).

The given expression is \((y-4)^2+(x-7)^2\).

Hence it is the square of the distance from \((x,y)\) to the fixed point \((7,4)\).

Write \(x=4+2\cos\theta\) and \(y=2\sin\theta\), where \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi\).

Then \((y-4)^2+(x-7)^2=(2\sin\theta-4)^2+(2\cos\theta-3)^2\).

Expanding gives \(4\sin^2\theta-16\sin\theta+16+4\cos^2\theta-12\cos\theta+9\).

Using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\), the expression becomes \(29-12\cos\theta-16\sin\theta\).

Now \(12\cos\theta+16\sin\theta\leq\sqrt{12^2+16^2}=20\).

Equality is possible when \(\cos\theta=\dfrac35\) and \(\sin\theta=\dfrac45\), which lies in the allowed interval.

Therefore, the minimum value is \(m=29-20=9\).

For the maximum, find the minimum of \(12\cos\theta+16\sin\theta\) on \([0,\pi]\).

Its derivative is \(-12\sin\theta+16\cos\theta\).

The interior critical point satisfies \(\tan\theta=\dfrac43\), and it gives the maximum value \(20\), not the minimum.

At \(\theta=0\), the value is \(12\).

At \(\theta=\pi\), the value is \(-12\).

Hence the minimum value is \(-12\), attained at \(\theta=\pi\).

Therefore, the maximum value of the original expression is \(M=29-(-12)=41\).

Thus \(M^2-m^2=41^2-9^2\).

Using \(a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)\), we get \((41-9)(41+9)=32\times50=1600\).

Hence the required answer is \(1600\).

questions.question:
If ft=∫0π2xdx1-cos2tsin2x,0<t<π, then ∫0π2π2dtf(t) is equal to  ______.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(f(t)=\int_0^\pi \frac{2x}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}dx\).

Since \( \frac{1}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x} \) remains same when \(x\) is replaced by \(\pi-x\),

we use the property \( \int_0^\pi xg(\sin x)dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^\pi g(\sin x)dx \).

So \(f(t)=2\cdot \frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^\pi \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}\).

Hence \(f(t)=\pi\int_0^\pi \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}\).

Now \( \int_0^\pi \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}=2\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x} \).

Using the standard result \( \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{dx}{1-a^2\sin^2 x}=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{1-a^2}} \),

we get \( \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt{1-\cos^2 t}} \).

Since \(0<t<\pi\), \( \sqrt{1-\cos^2 t}=|\sin t|=\sin t \).

Therefore \( \int_0^\pi \frac{dx}{1-\cos^2 t\sin^2 x}=\frac{\pi}{\sin t} \).

So \(f(t)=\pi\cdot \frac{\pi}{\sin t}=\frac{\pi^2}{\sin t}\).

Now \( \frac{\pi^2}{f(t)}=\frac{\pi^2}{\frac{\pi^2}{\sin t}}=\sin t \).

Therefore \( \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\pi^2}{f(t)}dt=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin t\,dt \).

Hence \( \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\sin t\,dt=[-\cos t]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=1 \).

questions.question:
If \(1+\frac{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}}{2 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{5-2 \sqrt{6}}{18}+\frac{9 \sqrt{3}-11 \sqrt{2}}{36 \sqrt{3}}+\frac{49-20 \sqrt{6}}{180}+\ldots\) upto \(\infty=2+\left(\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}+1\right) \log _e\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are integers with \(\operatorname{gcd}(a, b)=1\), then \(11 a+18 b\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(x=\sqrt3-\sqrt2\)

\(S=1+\frac{x}{2\sqrt3}+\frac{x^2}{18}+\frac{x^3}{36\sqrt3}+\frac{x^4}{180}+\cdots\)

Put \(\frac{x}{\sqrt3}=t\), where \(x=\sqrt3-\sqrt2\).

So, \(t=\frac{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\)

Now, \(S=1+\frac{t}{2}+\frac{t^2}{6}+\frac{t^3}{12}+\frac{t^4}{20}+\cdots\)

\(S=1+\frac{t}{1\cdot2}+\frac{t^2}{2\cdot3}+\frac{t^3}{3\cdot4}+\frac{t^4}{4\cdot5}+\cdots\)

Since \(\frac{1}{n(n+1)}=\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+1}\), we get

\(S=1+t\left(1-\frac{1}{2}\right)+t^2\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right)+t^3\left(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}\right)+t^4\left(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}\right)+\cdots\)

\(S=\left(1+t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{t^4}{4}+\cdots\right)-\left(\frac{t}{2}+\frac{t^2}{3}+\frac{t^3}{4}+\frac{t^4}{5}+\cdots\right)\)

\(S=2+\left(t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{t^4}{4}+\cdots\right)-\frac{1}{t}\left(t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{t^4}{4}+\cdots\right)\)

Using \(t+\frac{t^2}{2}+\frac{t^3}{3}+\cdots=-\log_e(1-t)\), we get

\(S=2+\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)(-\log_e(1-t))\)

\(S=2+\left(\frac{1}{t}-1\right)\log_e(1-t)\)

Now, \(1-t=1-\frac{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}=\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\)

and \(\frac{1}{t}-1=\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}-1=\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}\)

So, \(S=2+\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3-\sqrt2}\log_e\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\right)\)

\(S=2+(\sqrt6+2)\log_e\left(\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}\right)\)

\(S=2+\frac{\sqrt6+2}{2}\log_e\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\)

\(S=2+\left(\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}+1\right)\log_e\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)\)

Comparing with \(2+\left(\sqrt{\frac{b}{a}}+1\right)\log_e\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)\), we get

\(a=2\) and \(b=3\)

Therefore, \(11a+18b=11(2)+18(3)\)

\(=22+54=76\)

questions.question:
Let a line perpendicular to the line 2x-y=10 touch the parabola y2=4(x-9) at the point \(P\). The distance of the point \(P\) from the centre of the circle x2+y2-14x-8y+56=0 is  _______. 

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The slope of \(2x-y=10\) is \(2\).

\(\therefore\) the slope of the perpendicular tangent is \(m=-\dfrac12\).

For \(y^2=4(x-9)\), the point of contact of a tangent of slope \(m\) is \(\left(9+\dfrac{1}{m^2},\dfrac{2}{m}\right)\).

At \(m=-\dfrac12\), \(P=\left(9+4,-4\right)=(13,-4)\).

The circle is \(x^2+y^2-14x-8y+56=0\).

\(\Rightarrow (x-7)^2+(y-4)^2=9\)

\(\therefore\) its centre is \(C=(7,4)\).

\(PC=\sqrt{(13-7)^2+(-4-4)^2}\)

\(PC=\sqrt{36+64}=10\)

\(\therefore\) the required distance is \(10\)

questions.question:
Let the mean and the standard deviation of the probability distribution

be μ and σ, respectively. If σ-μ=2, then σ+μ is equal to ________.

 

[JEE Main 2024, 5 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The total probability is \(1\).

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{1}{3}+k+\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{1}{4}=1\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow k=1-\dfrac{4+2+3}{12}=\dfrac{1}{4}\)

The mean is

\(\displaystyle \mu=\alpha\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}+1\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}+0\cdot\dfrac{1}{6}-3\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow \mu=\dfrac{\alpha}{3}-\dfrac{1}{2}\)

Also, \(E(X^2)=\alpha^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}+1\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}+9\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{\alpha^2}{3}+\dfrac{5}{2}\)

\(\displaystyle \sigma^2=E(X^2)-\mu^2\)

The condition \(\sigma-\mu=2\) gives \(\sigma=\mu+2\).

\(\displaystyle \dfrac{\alpha^2}{3}+\dfrac{5}{2}-\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{3}-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{3}+\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow \alpha(\alpha-6)=0\)

If \(\alpha=0\), the table assigns both \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{6}\) to the same event \(X=0\), so it does not define a probability function.

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow \alpha=6\)

\(\displaystyle \mu=\dfrac{6}{3}-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{3}{2}\)

\(\displaystyle \sigma=\mu+2=\dfrac{7}{2}\)

\(\displaystyle \sigma+\mu=\dfrac{7}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}=5\)

The required value is \(5\).
